newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sale of Brazil power firm stake to go ahead today.
newsitem.headline: Sale of Brazil power firm stake to go ahead today.

text.p: Brazil's Federal District plans to proceed today with its planned sale of an 18.37 percent stake in power distributor Companhia Energetica de Brasilia (CEB), a Rio de Janeiro bolsa spokeswoman said.
A spokeswoman said the sale has not been interrupted by delays in the privatization auction of a 45-percent controlling stake in state mining giant Cia Vale do Rio Doce.
The federal district plans to auction 540.97 million preferred stock at a minimum price of 135.03 reais per 1,000 shares at 1315 local/1615 GMT/1215 EDT on the Rio stock exchange.
The CVRD selloff was slated for Tuesday morning but was reset for today after Brazilian courts granted a slew of injunctions suspending the auction.
The government must overturn several injunctions in order to pull off CVRD auction.
The CEB shares auction, which has been joined by investors aiming to sell off an added one million shares, is to take place as scheduled despite the CVRD selloff delays.

The federal district owns a 79.48 percent controlling stake in CEB, while district-owned companies hold 12.15 percent of the firm and federal power holding Eletrobras, pension funds and private investors own the rest.
